GPU-accelerated Leiden or Louvain community detection on an igraph

leiden_clustering_gpu.Rd

GPU counterpart of bixverse::leiden_clustering(). The level-0 local moving runs on the GPU; the coarser levels, the Leiden refinement and the aggregation stay on the CPU. Graphs below 50,000 nodes, or with a node of degree above 512, run fully on the CPU with coloured local moving, as the kernel launches cost more than they save there. On one device the partition depends on seed only, but it is not identical to the CPU result: the GPU accepts moves with an order-free rule instead of the CPU's sequential re-check. Communities are numbered by size, 1 being the largest.

Usage

leiden_clustering_gpu(
  graph,
  resolution = 1,
  algorithm = c("leiden", "louvain"),
  beta = 0.01,
  n_iterations = NULL,
  min_gain = 0,
  local_moving = c("queue", "coloured"),
  seed = 42L
)

Arguments

graph

igraph. Undirected. If it has an edge attribute weight, it is used, otherwise all edges get weight 1.

resolution

Numeric. Modularity resolution parameter. Higher values give more communities.

algorithm

String. One of c("leiden", "louvain").

beta

Numeric. Randomness of the Leiden refinement merges. Ignored for Louvain.

n_iterations

Optional integer. Number of full iterations, each starting from the previous partition. A negative value iterates until the partition is stable. If NULL, 5L for Leiden and 2L for Louvain.

min_gain

Numeric. With a negative n_iterations, also stop once an iteration gains no more than this in modularity.

local_moving

String. One of c("queue", "coloured"). Applies to the coarser levels only; level 0 always runs the coloured moves on the GPU.

seed

Integer. Random seed.

Value

Integer vector with the community of each node (1-based, 1 is the largest community).

References

Traag, Waltman & van Eck, Sci Rep, 2019; Blondel, et al., J Stat Mech, 2008
